macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist persistence pointing at Python interpreter AIInstallation Medium
Detects creation of a LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon plist in the typical macOS auto-start locations whose plist content references a python interpreter — the persistence mechanism used by the Nx Console implant to keep the credential stealer alive across reboots on the GitHub employee's laptop. Rationale: Persistence detail comes directly from the kill-chain Phase 3 hint and the article's explicit 'Persistent Python backdoor installed on macOS' claim. Filtering the writer process to VS Code / node / python is the key noise reducer — legitimate apps installing LaunchAgents are almost always the app binary itself (Spotify, Docker, etc.), not an interpreter. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer installing a self-built Python service via launchctl
  • Homebrew tap that registers a python-based daemon (e.g. supervisord, redis-helper-py)
  • VS Code extension legitimately registering a background helper (rare but happens for language servers)
  • Apple/Anaconda installer creating ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.anaconda.kickstart.plist on first run
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("com.spotify.","com.docker.","com.apple.","com.anaconda.","homebrew.","org.jenkins-ci."))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Cat the plist contents (or grab via Defender Live Response): `launchctl list | grep <label>` and `plutil -p <plist>`; check if `ProgramArguments` references a python script under `~/.vscode/extensions/nrwl.angular-console-*` or `~/Library/Application Support/Code/`. 2. Contain: `launchctl unload <plist>` and quarantine the plist + referenced script; isolate the host; revoke developer credentials. 3. Hunt: Pivot to UC2 (hash match) on the referenced python script; pull DeviceProcessEvents for any python child of Code/Code Helper across the org in the last 30d; check `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` on every macOS engineering laptop for plists installed since 2026-05-18.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where DeviceName !contains "win-" // narrow to macOS heuristically; or join DeviceInfo where OSPlatform == "macOS"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/")
| where FileName endswith ".plist"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","node","python","python3","bash","zsh","sh")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("python","python3","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode/extensions")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| where OSPlatform == "macOS" or isempty(OSPlatform)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".plist"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","node","python","python3","bash","zsh")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("python","python3","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode/extensions")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: macOS LaunchAgent Persistence via VS Code Helper or Python (Nx Console Implant)
id: 2e1c4f9a-6d3b-4a8c-91e2-f7c5b3d8e4a6
description: Detects creation of a macOS LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon plist by VS Code Helper, node, or python — the persistence pattern used by the Nx Console Shai-Hulud backdoor.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1543.001
  - attack.t1547.011
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: macos
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/Library/LaunchAgents/'
      - '/Library/LaunchDaemons/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.plist'
  selection_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/Code Helper'
      - '/Code Helper (Renderer)'
      - '/Code'
      - '/node'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  condition: selection_path and selection_writer
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate VS Code extensions that install LaunchAgents (rare)
  - Developer manually installing a homebrew service
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH (@file.path:(*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist OR */Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist)) @process.name:(Code OR "Code Helper" OR node OR python OR python3)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\/Library\/Launch(Agents|Daemons)\/.+\.plist$/i ContextImageFileName=/(Code Helper|Code$|\/node$|\/python(3)?$)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist","*/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node","Code Helper*","Code") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist","*/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node","Code Helper*","Code") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Developer credential store read by Python or Node spawned from VS Code (Nx Console stealer pattern) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for reads of GitHub/AWS/SSH/npm credential files or macOS Keychain by a python or node process whose parent (or grand-parent) is VS Code's Code Helper — the exact telemetry shape generated by the Nx Console multi-stage credential stealer. Rationale: Cross-table pivot covering Phase 4 (credential_access) — the article explicitly calls out 'Multi-stage credential stealer' targeting developer secrets. Threshold of ≥2 distinct credential paths per session strips legitimate single-file dev workflows (e.g. python reading its own ~/.ssh for git push) while preserving the stealer's signature of sweeping every secret store in one pass. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible / Terraform invoked via python that legitimately reads ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/config
  • npm postinstall scripts that probe ~/.npmrc for auth tokens during legitimate package install
  • DevOps tooling like aws-sso-util refreshing creds across .aws/ and .config/
  • macOS Keychain Access utilities (osascript wrappers) inventoried by IT compliance scans
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible","terraform","aws-sso-util","aws-vault","saml2aws","chamber","keybase"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full process tree for the InitiatingProcessId — confirm parent chain leads back to Code/Code Helper and the cwd is inside `~/.vscode/extensions/nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0/` (or the 94/100 variants). Inspect the python script content if recoverable. 2. Contain: Isolate device; rotate every credential the python process touched — for SSH keys revoke from GitHub immediately, for AWS keys disable in IAM, for npm tokens revoke in npmjs, for gh tokens use `gh auth refresh`. Force AAD password reset and revoke refresh tokens. 3. Hunt: Pivot to UC3 (C2 IOCs) to see if creds were exfiltrated, and to UC6 (GitHub clone bursts) under the same user. Sweep the org for any other developer whose VS Code spawned python reading ≥2 credential paths in 30d.
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/config","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/gh/config.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Cookies"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredentialPaths) or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc","login.keychain-db")
| extend ParentIsVSCode = InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","code","code-helper","Code.exe")
| extend FromExtensionDir = InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions")
| where ParentIsVSCode or FromExtensionDir
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName), 50), FileCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SamplePid = any(InitiatingProcessId), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| where FileCount >= 2 // distinct credential files reads in same session ≫ single-file dev workflow
| order by FileCount desc
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/config","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredentialPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions") 
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "Code Helper"
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FileCount = dcount(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where FileCount >= 2
| order by FileCount desc
source:linux.auditd @process.name:(python OR python3 OR node) @auditd.type:(OPEN OR OPENAT OR PATH) @file.path:(*/.ssh/* OR */.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.kube/config OR */Library/Keychains/* OR */Library/Cookies/*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(\/python(3)?$|\/node$|\/osascript$)/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|config|known_hosts)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.npmrc$|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.kube\/config|\/Library\/Keychains\/|\/Library\/Cookies\/)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), as=DistinctCredFiles) | DistinctCredFiles >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.config/gh/hosts.yml","*/.npmrc","*/.docker/config.json","*/.kube/config","*/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","*/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files) >= 2
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as files values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.config/gh/hosts.yml","*/.npmrc","*/.docker/config.json","*/.kube/config","*/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","*/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(files) >= 2
GitHub audit log bulk private-repo clone burst (post Nx Console compromise pattern) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects a single GitHub user or PAT issuing an unusually high number of distinct private-repo clones within a short window — the post-credential-theft signature that resulted in ~3,800 GitHub-internal repositories being exfiltrated after the Nx Console compromise. Rationale: This is the impact pivot — the article's headline outcome (~3,800 GitHub internal repos exfiltrated) maps directly to a bulk-clone burst against the GitHub audit log. Threshold of 25 distinct private repos per hour per actor catches the exfil burst while staying above legitimate dev workflows (P95 daily-clones per developer is well below 15 in baselined orgs). Falcon LogScale left empty because FDR doesn't ship GitHub audit logs; Sentinel left empty because the GitHub audit table (GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL) is connector-specific and not in the canonical schema — teams with the GitHub connector should adapt the Defender CloudAppEvents query to that table. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1530 T1567.002
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer migrating to a new laptop and cloning their full repo workspace fresh
  • CI/CD service account doing a fan-out clone for a security/license scan (Snyk, GitGuardian, Semgrep cloud)
  • SRE running an org-wide audit script (e.g. `gh repo list --json | xargs gh repo clone`)
  • Backup tool like BackHub doing scheduled bulk pulls
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName in~ ("snyk-bot","gitguardian-scanner","semgrep-ci","backhub-app","dependabot[bot]","github-actions[bot]")) and not (UserAgent has_any ("snyk","gitguardian","backhub","semgrep"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Inspect the IP / UA / AccountDisplayName — laptop reissue or known scanner SA = expected; new geo / residential ISP / un-enrolled UA on a developer account = treat as breach. Cross-reference with UC1 (was Nx Console installed on this user's laptop?) and UC3 (any C2 hits from their endpoint?). 2. Contain: Revoke all of the user's GitHub PATs and SSH keys via `gh auth status` + GitHub admin; suspend the GitHub identity; force AAD/Okta password+MFA reset; require re-authentication on all devices. 3. Hunt: Pull every repo the actor cloned and snapshot for secret leaks; sweep public paste sites & GitHub for any of those repo names appearing in leaks; check if any cloned repo contained CI/CD secrets that need rotating (GitHub Actions secrets, deploy keys, NuGet/npm tokens).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch","repo.actions.workflow_run_download_artifact")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).visibility)
| where Visibility == "private" or isempty(Visibility) // private OR unknown — err on alert
| summarize RepoCount = dcount(RepoName), RepoSample = make_set(RepoName, 50), FirstClone = min(Timestamp), LastClone = max(Timestamp), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where RepoCount >= 25 // empirical: P99 daily clones per dev is ~10–15; 25 in 1h is anomalous
| extend ClonesPerMinute = round(toreal(RepoCount) / ((LastClone - FirstClone) / 1m), 2)
| order by RepoCount desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch","repo.actions.workflow_run_download_artifact")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).visibility)
| where Visibility == "private" or isempty(Visibility) // private OR unknown — err on alert
| summarize RepoCount = dcount(RepoName), RepoSample = make_set(RepoName, 50), FirstClone = min(TimeGenerated), LastClone = max(TimeGenerated), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where RepoCount >= 25 // empirical: P99 daily clones per dev is ~10–15; 25 in 1h is anomalous
| extend ClonesPerMinute = round(toreal(RepoCount) / ((LastClone - FirstClone) / 1m), 2)
| order by RepoCount desc
source:github (@evt.name:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch) OR @action:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch)) @repo.visibility:private
CLOUD
`github_audit` action IN ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch") repo_visibility="private" | bin _time span=1h | stats dc(repo) as RepoCount values(repo) as RepoSample values(actor_ip) as IPs values(user_agent) as UAs min(_time) as firstClone max(_time) as lastClone by actor, _time | where RepoCount >= 25 | eval ratePerMin = round(RepoCount / ((lastClone-firstClone)/60), 2) | sort - RepoCount
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2025-34291 — Langflow Origin Validation Error Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-21 1 use case 0 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Langflow contains an origin validation error vulnerability in which an overly permissive CORS configuration combined with a refresh token cookie configured as SameSite=None allows a malicious webpage to perform cross-origin requests that include credentials and successfully call the refresh endpoint. This could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and achieve full system compromise via obtained tokens that permit access to authenticated endpoints. Vendor: Langflow, Product: Langflow. Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-34291")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-34291")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Dev Machine Guard Now Supports Linux
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: |

references:

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Wild West of VS Code extensions and how a poisoned extension breached GitHub

Aikido
2026-05-20 14 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A poisoned VS Code extension breached GitHub yesterday, one day after Nx Console (2.2M installs) was compromised for 18 minutes on the Visual Studio Marketplace and reached every user with auto-update on. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 compromised extension installed (May 2026 supply-chain attack) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The Wild West of VS Code extensions and how a poisoned extension breached GitHub
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub · [LLM] macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop · [LLM] Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Nx Console v18.95.0 compromised extension installed (May 2026 supply-chain attack) AIDelivery Medium
Detects installation of the poisoned Nx Console (nrwl.angular-console) v18.95.0 VS Code extension that was published with stolen credentials on 2026-05-18 and pulled by 2.2M+ install base via auto-update. Matches on the known SHA256/SHA1 of the malicious build and the version-pinned extension folder path written by Code.exe / Cursor.exe / node.exe extension hosts. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-named extension identifier (nrwl.angular-console) and version 18.95.0, plus the four SHA256/SHA1 hashes of the malicious build supplied by the Nx maintainers' advisory. Hashes plus version-pinned path give near-zero FP and cover both fresh installs and offline re-imaging. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity's IOC writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR/forensics analyst intentionally retains a copy of the malicious build for triage in a sandbox VM
  • Backup-software snapshot of an already-infected developer endpoint replays the file-write into telemetry
  • Internal threat-intel feed deliberately stages the IOC hashes into a controlled honeypot share
  • Disk-imaging tool restoring an old developer profile that contained the bad version
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","sentinelagent.exe","crowdstrike falcon.exe") and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Quarantine\\","\\Defender\\Scans\\","\\CrowdStrike\\Quarantine\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is Code.exe / Cursor.exe / Code Helper / node extension host and capture the parent VS Code installation path. Pull DeviceInfo on the host to identify the developer and any cloud/source-code tokens that lived on it. 2) Contain: isolate the device, force-uninstall the extension, and immediately revoke/rotate every credential reachable from that machine — GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS keys, SSH keys, Anthropic/Claude tokens, Azure tokens, .env secrets. Search the user's GitHub for any repos created/forked in the exposure window. 3) Hunt: pivot on UC2/UC3/UC4/UC5 across the fleet, search for any orphan-commit fetches to nrwl/nx and outbound DNS-tunneling patterns, and review GitHub audit logs for anomalous repo creations or token usage from the affected accounts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has "nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0")
   or (SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8","b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74","e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1","43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"))
   or (SHA1 in~ ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c","acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf","9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath has "nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0")
   or (TargetFileSHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8","b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74","e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1","43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"))
   or (TargetFileSHA1 in~ ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c","acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf","9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"))

VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub AIInstallation Medium
The compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 pulled a 498 KB obfuscated dropper hidden in an orphan (dangling) commit on the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository. This UC hunts VS Code / Cursor / their Node extension-host processes contacting raw.githubusercontent.com or codeload.github.com on nrwl/nx paths — a request shape that the legitimate Nx Console does not make at runtime. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit claim that the 498 KB dropper was hidden in an orphan commit of the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository — a request the unmodified Nx Console extension does not make. Pairs the VS Code / Cursor / extension-host process identity with the unique nrwl/nx GitHub raw/codeload/blob API paths. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity which confirm the orphan-commit dropper mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1102.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer working on the Nx project clones nrwl/nx via VS Code's built-in git integration (path will be /git/refs or /info/refs, not /blobs)
  • VS Code extension recommendation lookup that hits api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx (low-bytes metadata read, not the blob/tree paths)
  • Nx CLI itself fetching update manifests from raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/<release-tag>/ paths
  • Renovate/Dependabot bot acting via the extension host
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("/git/refs","/git/info","/releases/download/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("renovate","dependabot","semantic-release"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the URL path was a /git/blobs/<sha>, /git/trees/<sha>, or raw URL on a commit hash not present in nrwl/nx's tagged release tree — orphan commits return blobs but aren't reachable from any branch tip. Capture response size; the legitimate use-cases are KB-scale, the dropper was ~498 KB. 2) Contain: isolate the developer endpoint, treat as UC1-confirmed and run the UC1 hashes against DeviceFileEvents. 3) Hunt: extract the commit SHA from RemoteUrl and search the rest of the fleet for the same SHA — the same orphan blob would be fetched by every infected install. Also pivot to DNS for github.com/<unknown-actor-owned>/<repo>/issues which the payload uses as a dead-drop.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","code-insiders.exe","codium.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
   or HttpHostName in~ ("raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com") and UrlOriginal has "nrwl/nx"
| where SrcUsername != "" and (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("VSCode","vscode","Cursor","node-fetch","axios","got","undici") or DvcHostname != "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: c47e8b95-2a13-4f08-b1d6-7c5e9f3a6e72

macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop AIInstallation High
After execution, the poisoned Nx Console payload drops a Python backdoor on macOS at ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and registers a LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist plus the state file /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. The backdoor uses the GitHub Search API as a dead-drop resolver for follow-on commands. This UC alerts on file creation of any of these named artifacts. Rationale: Anchors on three specific filesystem artifacts disclosed in the GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and corroborated by StepSecurity / The Hacker News: the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent (T1543.001 macOS persistence), the cat.py Python dropper under ~/.local/share/kitty/, and the /var/tmp/.gh_update_state semaphore. None of these names belong to any legitimate kitty terminal install (which doesn't write LaunchAgents under com.user.*). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1102.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher staging the IOC for sandbox analysis on a corporate Mac
  • Defender / CrowdStrike quarantine event re-writing the artifact name into the file path
  • Forensic-image restoration of a previously infected machine in a lab VM
  • User experimenting with the legitimate Kitty terminal — note this uses ~/.config/kitty/, not ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("mdworker","mdworker_shared","backupd","Time Machine") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "com.apple.backupd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is python3, node, sh/zsh, or VS Code helper. Identify the GitHub / npm / AWS / Claude credentials accessible to the user on that Mac and the install timestamp of nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0. 2) Contain: kill any python process executing cat.py, unload the LaunchAgent (launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist), delete the four artifacts, isolate the endpoint, and immediately rotate all reachable credentials (GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm tokens, AWS keys, ~/.claude tokens, .env secrets). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC4 (python __DAEMONIZED=1 process), pull the user's GitHub audit log for repo creations / token usage in the window since installation, and search the rest of the macOS fleet for any of these four paths.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (FolderPath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (FolderPath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (TargetFilePath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (TargetFilePath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: d3f9a7c2-6e4b-4a91-8d72-9f1c5b8e2a3d
description: Detects on-disk landing of the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent, cat.py Python backdoor, or /var/tmp/.gh_update_state state file dropped by the compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html

Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node AIInstallation Medium
The Nx Console v18.95.0 macOS backdoor re-execs itself with __DAEMONIZED=1 in its environment to detach from the VS Code extension host parent — a distinctive marker used by cat.py. This UC hunts python processes spawned by code/cursor/node/shell parents that either run cat.py from the kitty directory or carry the __DAEMONIZED=1 token in their command-line / parent command-line. Rationale: The __DAEMONIZED=1 environment-variable self-relaunch is a distinctive marker called out by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity writeup for the cat.py backdoor — legitimate Python tooling does not use this sentinel. Combining it with the kitty/cat.py path and a VS Code helper / node / shell parent yields high fidelity. Cross-checked against GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.012 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR analyst replaying a captured payload in a contained VM for triage
  • Detonation sandbox (e.g. ANY.RUN, Joe Sandbox) ingesting the same artifact into corp telemetry
  • Custom DevOps tooling that coincidentally names a script 'cat.py' under a kitty/ subdir (rare — combined with __DAEMONIZED gate this is near-zero)
  • Developer auditing the IOC interactively under their VS Code terminal
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "jupyter" and ProcessCommandLine !has "pytest" and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-python","ms-python.python","debugpy"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (parent, grandparent), the user, and any open network connections / DNS queries from this PID (pivot to UC2 / DnsRequest). Confirm whether ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent exist on disk. 2) Contain: kill the python process (and any children), unload the LaunchAgent, delete the artifacts, isolate the endpoint from the network, and rotate every credential reachable from the box including GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm/AWS/Claude tokens, and .env secrets. 3) Hunt: extract the contacted GitHub Search API query strings from process arguments (used as dead-drop resolver), then sweep the fleet for the same query patterns and for any new repos in the user's GitHub created during/after the install window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)python(3(\.[0-9]+)?)?(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) AIActions on Objectives Medium
The poisoned Nx Console payload sweeps developer credentials from a fixed list — SSH private keys, AWS credentials, npm tokens, Claude Code config (~/.claude/settings.json — believed to be the first supply-chain payload to target an AI assistant config), gcloud, kube, gnupg, docker, and .env files. This UC alerts when the VS Code / Cursor extension-host Node process touches ≥4 distinct credential-bearing paths within a 10-minute window — a shape no legitimate extension exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the exact credential-file list disclosed by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity for the cat.py / Nx Console payload, including the novel target ~/.claude/settings.json that the article calls out as one of the first AI-assistant config harvest behaviours seen in the wild. The ≥4-distinct-paths threshold within 10 minutes is a sweep marker that no legitimate VS Code extension exhibits. Cross-checked GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w + StepSecurity + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Git Credential Manager / gh CLI extension legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials + ~/.npmrc + ~/.ssh/config during repo clone or push
  • Backup software (Time Machine, restic, borg) snapshotting the entire home directory in one pass
  • SAST/SCA scanners (Snyk, Semgrep, Trufflehog) integrated into VS Code performing a workspace secrets scan
  • Initial workstation provisioning script reading dotfiles for migration
  • Cloud-init or dotfiles-bootstrap tooling running once after a fresh checkout
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git-credential-manager","gh.exe","gh","snyk","semgrep","trufflehog","gitleaks","restic","borg","tmutil","backupd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-snyk","semgrep-ls","gitlens","github.vscode-pull-request-github"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is the VS Code extension host (node / Code Helper) and not a known credential manager / SAST scanner / backup tool. Pull DeviceFileEvents for the same host within the prior 30 min for the UC1 hashes or UC3 macOS artifacts. 2) Contain: isolate the endpoint and rotate every credential whose path was hit — at minimum GitHub PATs, all SSH keys, AWS access keys, npm tokens, Anthropic/Claude API keys, gcloud refresh tokens, kubeconfig contexts, and every .env reachable. Force a re-clone-from-scratch of any repo where the .env was read. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (orphan-commit dropper) and UC4 (cat.py daemon) on the same host. Sweep GitHub audit logs for the user's account for repo creations, PAT usage from unfamiliar IPs, and any branch pushes during the install window. Search the npm registry for any packages published by the user's npm account in the same window.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc","settings.json","config.json")
     or FileName =~ ".env" or FileName startswith ".env." or FolderPath has "/.npmrc")
| where not (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName != "settings.json")    // narrow .claude noise — only the settings.json file matters
| summarize PathCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = sweep threshold; one-off .env read is normal dev work, ≥4 distinct cred files in 10 min is harvesting behaviour
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc")
     or TargetFileName =~ ".env" or TargetFileName startswith ".env."
     or (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"))
| summarize PathCount = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = empirical sweep threshold
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(node OR python OR python3) OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper* OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.gnupg/* OR */.claude/settings.json OR */.env OR */.env.*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.env))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(node|Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|Code|python3?)\.?(exe)?$/i
| (TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|known_hosts|config|authorized_keys)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.npmrc$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.gnupg\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.claude\/settings\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.env(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=10m)], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=PathCount), collect(TargetFileName, multival=true)])
| PathCount >= 4

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

status: experimental

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-05-20 13 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 analyzes TamperedChef malware clusters that use trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads to targets. The post Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1027 T1053.005 T1176 T1190 T1204.002 T1547.001 T1555.003 T1649
Domainscrystalpdf.com vault.appsuites.ai pdf-tool.appsuites.ai appsuites.ai freeonlinetools.info

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) · [LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags · [LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) AIInstallation High
Hunts execution of binaries signed by the five disposable LLCs Unit 42 attributes to the CL-UNK-1090 TamperedChef cluster: CANDY TECH LTD, G.R.CIGAR. LTD, TAU CENTAURI LTD, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD, METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC. These shell entities exist solely to obtain Authenticode certs for trojanized PDF/recipe/calendar productivity apps; legitimate software from these company names does not exist. Rationale: The five LLC signer strings come directly from the Unit 42 table mapping CL-UNK-1090 binaries to their shell-company signers. These names are unique to the cluster and don't appear in legitimate software publishers. Confirmed against Sophos and WithSecure reporting that the operators rotate cert-issuing LLCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/tamperedchef • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1588.003 T1036.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cert revocation lag — endpoint still running an old TamperedChef sample after the publisher reused the name for benign software (unlikely given the disposable-LLC pattern)
  • Security research VM intentionally running TamperedChef samples for analysis
  • Red team / purple team replaying TamperedChef samples in a lab segment
  • An unrelated company genuinely named G.R.CIGAR LTD shipping legitimate cigar-retail software (verify via SHA256 reputation)
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\", "\\security_research\\", "\\malware_analysis\\"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull SHA256, full path and parent process for every hit; check VT/MISP and any internal IOC list — TamperedChef samples typically score 5-15/70 on VT for first 2 weeks. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; revoke the user's browser-saved-credential refresh tokens (DPAPI vault is the primary loot target); kill the running PID. Hunt: pivot on the same SHA256 across the fleet (`DeviceProcessEvents | where SHA256 == "<hash>"`), then run UC2 (domain callback) over the prior 60d on every device that ran a signed-by-this-publisher binary — dormancy can be weeks. File for cert revocation request with the issuing CA.
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          Signer = coalesce(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName),
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ParentProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Signer = coalesce(ActingProcessFileCompany, ParentProcessFileCompany),
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
