TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts host network egress and DNS to the article's named TamperedChef infrastructure: appsuites.ai (including pdf-tool / vault subdomains), crystalpdf.com, freeonlinetools.info. These are the trojanized-installer download hosts and the dormant-then-activate C2 used by CL-CRI-1089 / CL-UNK-1090. Rationale: appsuites.ai, pdf-tool.appsuites.ai, vault.appsuites.ai, crystalpdf.com and freeonlinetools.info are the article's named distribution/C2 hosts; fullpdf.com added from Sophos corroboration. These are unique campaign-specific domains — no legitimate business overlap. Any callback after the dormancy window is high-confidence post-install activation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/tamperedchef-malware-disguised-as-fake.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tamperedchef-infostealer-delivered-through-fraudulent-pdf-editor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher manually browsing the campaign sites for analysis — flag once, then add researcher device to allowlist
  • Threat-intel platform sandbox fetching the domains for enrichment (e.g. VT, ANY.RUN) — exclude by source IP range
  • Web-proxy product re-fetching for category lookup — exclude by InitiatingProcessFileName (e.g. ZScalerClient.exe)
  • User clicking a malvertised search result but the install never completes — still high-fidelity since the lure is malicious
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--load-extension","--remote-debugging-port"))
Response runbook
Triage: identify the process that initiated the connection — InitiatingProcessFileName + CompanyName tells you which trojanized app is on the host (AppSuite PDF / CrystalPDF / etc.). Pull the SHA256 and confirm against UC1 signers. Contain: isolate the host; force-revoke the user's browser refresh tokens (Edge/Chrome) and rotate any SSO password since DPAPI vault dump is the stealer's primary objective; uninstall the offending app and remove the scheduled-task persistence (see UC3 / UC4). Hunt: extend the DNS query backwards 90 days for the same domains — install can predate activation by weeks. Run UC1 across the fleet to catch dormant peers with the same signer.
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
  | extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
  | where Host in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Host endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Host endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "Network", Indicator = RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Query = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString))
  | where Query in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Query endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Query endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "DNS", Indicator = Query, RemoteIP = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".appsuites.ai" or DnsQuery endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (TamperedChefHosts) or DestinationHostName has_any (TamperedChefHosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, DnsQuery = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags AIInstallation High
Hunts the article's productivity-app installers (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) re-launching themselves with the activation flags --cm, --install, --enableupdate or --fullupdate. These flags are the documented switch from dormant-installed state to active stealer/C2 behaviour and have no legitimate productivity-software analogue. Rationale: Article names AppSuite PDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky and CrystalPDF as the trojanized productivity apps. Sophos/Acronis/SecurityOnline corroborate --cm as the documented activation argument and --enableupdate / --fullupdate / --install as the persistent-update flags; these strings don't appear in legitimate productivity-app installers and pair directly with the article's family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002 T1480
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Electron-based PDF tool with overlapping product name but different signer — verify against UC1 publisher list
  • Internal app-packaging team testing software-deployment scripts that re-use the --install flag literal — exclude by deployment-server device group
  • Malware-analysis sandbox detonating TamperedChef samples for research
  • User clean-install with legitimate --install on a same-named but unrelated tool — rare given the campaign-specific product names
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "REINSTALL")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the binary signer matches one of the five shell-company publishers from UC1 — if so, this is the dormant-to-active activation moment. Pull the SHA256, full command line (especially the --cm payload if present), and parent process. Contain: kill the activated process, isolate the host, force-revoke the user's browser-saved-cred refresh tokens and Microsoft 365 sessions (stealer-stage targets DPAPI vault and cookies). Hunt: across the fleet for the same product name regardless of cmdline (UC1 / signer hunt) — those are the dormant peers. Pull DeviceFileEvents for files written by this PID to identify the dropped stealer module.
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)
   or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Signer = ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName,
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);

title: TamperedChef Productivity-App Activation Flags
id: 6c3e8a2d-4d6b-4cad-bf5c-7b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects TamperedChef trojanized productivity apps (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) launching with documented activation/update flags --cm, --enableupdate, --fullupdate, --install.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-tampered-chef-clusters/
  - https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1480
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AppSuitePDF.exe'
      - '\AppSuite.exe'
      - '\CrystalPDF.exe'
      - '\Calendaromatic.exe'
      - '\JustAskJacky.exe'
      - '\PDFEditor.exe'
      - '\ManualFinder.exe'
      - '\RecipeLister.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--cm '
      - '--cm='
      - '--enableupdate'
      - '--fullupdate'
      - '--install '
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\AppSuite*.exe OR *\\CrystalPDF.exe OR *\\Calendaromatic.exe OR *\\JustAskJacky.exe OR *\\appsuite*.exe OR *\\crystalpdf.exe OR *\\calendaromatic.exe OR *\\justaskjacky.exe)) (@CommandLine:*--cm* OR @CommandLine:*--enableupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--fullupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--install*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(AppSuite(PDF)?|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|PDFEditor|ManualFinder|RecipeLister)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(--cm[=\s]|--enableupdate|--fullupdate|--install\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) AIInstallation High
Hunts the article-corroborated TamperedChef persistence pattern: schtasks.exe importing a freshly-dropped task.xml that registers a recurring task launching wscript/cscript against an obfuscated JS such as appsuite-print.js. Combines the file-drop, the schtasks /create /xml import and the resulting script-host execution to catch the persistence handoff. Rationale: task.xml drop + schtasks /create /xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) is the TamperedChef persistence handoff documented by SecurityOnline and Acronis corroborating the article's CL-CRI-1089 trojanized-app behaviour. The 24h join window catches the schedule registration paired to the subsequent script-host launch, dramatically reducing FP vs schtasks alone. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/ • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate enterprise software using XML-defined scheduled tasks installed from %TEMP% during MSI rollout — exclude by SCCM/Intune deployer parent
  • Backup or update agents creating recurring JS-driven tasks (rare; verify product name is not on UC1 publisher list)
  • Developer running schtasks /create /xml against a local task.xml during testing — exclude by user/device dev-group
  • NodeJS/Electron app legitimately running .js with a productivity-themed name from %AppData% — verify signer
Suppression filter
and not (SchedParent in~ ("ccmexec.exe","TiWorker.exe","msiexec.exe") and SchedParentCompany has "Microsoft")
Response runbook
Triage: read the dropped task.xml (DeviceFileEvents query for the file) and inspect its <Actions> block — the malicious tasks call wscript/cscript on a JS file under the app's install dir or %AppData%. Confirm publisher matches UC1's shell-company list. Contain: delete the scheduled task (`schtasks /delete /tn <name>`), kill the running script host, isolate the host, rotate browser credentials. Hunt: pull DeviceFileEvents for all .xml task files dropped by the same parent process across the fleet and dump the corresponding .js bodies; pivot DeviceImageLoadEvents on the script host PIDs to surface any in-memory follow-on stealer modules. Run UC2 to find prior dormant C2 callbacks on each affected host.
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            SchedCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            SchedParentCompany = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let ScriptHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, ScriptCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DeviceName
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DeviceName, AccountName,
          SchedParent, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            SchedCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParentName = ParentProcessName,
            SchedParentCompany = ParentProcessFileCompany;
let ScriptHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ScriptCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = ParentProcessName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DvcHostname
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          SchedParentName, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*"/create"* AND *"/xml"*) (@CommandLine:*task.xml* OR @CommandLine:*AppSuite* OR @CommandLine:*CrystalPDF* OR @CommandLine:*Calendaromatic* OR @CommandLine:*JustAskJacky* OR @CommandLine:*appsuite-print.js*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/create", field=CommandLine)
| regex("/xml", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(task\\.xml|AppSuite|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|appsuite-print\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com AICommand & Control High
Hunts any developer endpoint resolving or connecting to check.git-service.com (or sibling subdomains under git-service.com), the credential-exfiltration host used by the TeamPCP Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain payload. The domain has no legitimate use — any hit is high-fidelity for the GitHub-breach campaign. Rationale: Domain check.git-service.com is the article's lead IOC; cross-checked via BleepingComputer and StepSecurity write-ups of the same Nx Console v18.95.0 / TeamPCP incident. Any DNS query for this name from a corporate endpoint indicates active credential exfiltration in progress. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/github-confirms-breach-of-3-800-repos-via-malicious-vscode-extension/ • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-internal-repositories-breached.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst triaging the IOC from a jump host (curl/dig/nslookup against the indicator)
  • IOC enrichment tooling (MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive) auto-resolving the domain for context
  • VirusTotal sandbox detonation traffic if VT IDS feed is ingested into the same DNS lake
  • Threat-intel vendor periodic re-resolution of historic IOCs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","nslookup.exe","dig.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("misp","opencti","thehive","virustotal","--ioc"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm which user, process, and parent process initiated the egress (InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName). If Code.exe, node.exe, or npx is in the chain treat as confirmed Nx Console infection on the workstation. 2. Contain: isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse / CS Network Containment, force-rotate every GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access key, 1Password recovery key, and HashiCorp Vault token bound to that user identity; revoke all GitHub SSH/OAuth grants for the user; invalidate active SSO sessions. 3. Hunt: pivot on AccountName/UserName across the last 30 days for additional egress to git-service.com siblings, recent `git clone` of internal repos from the user's PAT, and any new orphan-commit pushes the stolen token may have made.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "git-service.com" or RemoteIP in ("")
 | extend Source="NetworkEvent"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
 | where RemoteUrl has "git-service.com" or AdditionalFields has "git-service.com"
 | extend Source="DeviceEvent"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Name has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode, Source="DnsEvents"),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DestinationHostName has "git-service.com" or RequestURL has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DnsQuery has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName, Source="ImDnsActivity")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TeamPCP Nx Console payload SHA256 hash match on developer endpoints AIInstallation Medium
Direct hash-based detection for the four known Nx Console v18.95.0 malicious payload SHA256s — the 2,777-byte injected stub plus the dropped 498KB obfuscated stealer fetched from the nrwl/nx orphan commit. Any write or execution of these binaries on a corporate endpoint is unambiguous compromise. Rationale: Four SHA256s from the article's IOC block; campaign and payload behaviour cross-checked against the official nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and StepSecurity analysis. Hash matches on developer endpoints are unambiguous and warrant immediate isolation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox / detonation VM intentionally executing the known sample
  • Endpoint AV/EDR vendor lab machine running the sample for signature tuning
  • SOC reverse-engineering workstation handling the dropped 498KB stealer for IR analysis
  • Aikido / StepSecurity / similar SCA tool quarantining the sample in a controlled location
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("malware-sandbox-01","ir-analysis-vm","av-lab-01")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the user, parent VS Code process, and timestamp of first hash hit; check whether the device is a sandbox/RE box (allowlist if confirmed). 2. Contain: isolate the host immediately, capture memory if feasible, force rotation of all developer credentials (GitHub PAT, npm token, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, 1Password recovery key, HashiCorp Vault tokens) bound to the user, revoke all GitHub OAuth grants and active SSO sessions for that identity. 3. Hunt: pivot the SHA256 fleet-wide for prior sightings, search VS Code extension install telemetry for nrwl.angular-console v18.94.x / v18.95.0, audit GitHub Enterprise audit log for unusual `repo:clone` events from the user's PAT in the prior 30 days.

VS Code child process fetching payload from nrwl/nx orphan commit (Nx Console v18.95.0 dropper) AIInstallation High
Detects the post-install execution chain unique to the TeamPCP Nx Console compromise: a child process of VS Code (Code.exe / Code - Insiders.exe) invoking npx, node, cmd, or PowerShell with a command line that references either the malicious orphan commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 or raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx — the exact mechanism that pulls down the 498KB obfuscated stealer. Rationale: Pivots on the unique orphan-commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 (confirmed by the nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and Nx postmortem) plus the raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx fetch pattern — both are second-source-verified and have no legitimate use. The parent=Code.exe + child=npx/node + URL pattern is unique to the Nx Console v18.95.0 activation flow. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1195.002 T1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Reverse engineer manually re-fetching the orphan-commit blob for analysis from a triage workstation
  • DFIR tooling pulling the IOC from a sandboxed reproduction script
  • Threat intel team mirroring the orphan commit to a private repo for safekeeping (rare)
  • CTF or training exercise reproducing the published attack chain
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("svc-malware-research","svc-dfir") and DeviceName !in~ ("re-vm-01","sandbox-01")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the user, exact CommandLine, and downstream child processes spawned by the npx/node invocation — record the SHA256 of the dropped file in %TEMP% or ~/.npm/_npx. 2. Contain: isolate the workstation, kill the offending node process tree, rotate every developer credential bound to the user (GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS keys, Claude Code config, 1Password recovery, Vault tokens), revoke GitHub OAuth grants and active SSO sessions. 3. Hunt: enumerate all hosts with VS Code extension nrwl.angular-console v18.94.x–v18.95.0 installed, sweep for the four payload SHA256s, audit GitHub Enterprise audit log for `repo:clone` of internal repositories using the user's PAT in the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code Helper (Renderer)")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code")
| where FileName in~ ("npx.cmd","npx","node.exe","node","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx","github.com/nrwl/nx/raw","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

 | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Code.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\Code - Insiders.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\code" or ParentProcessName endswith "Code Helper"
 | where NewProcessName endswith "\\npx.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
 | where CommandLine has_any ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx","github.com/nrwl/nx/raw","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectAccount, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),

 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine)

references:

Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-collection burst pattern executed by the Nx Console v18.95.0 stealer: a single Code.exe or node.exe process touching five or more distinct credential/secret files (.env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.config/1Password) within a 5-minute window. The behaviour mirrors the published payload's documented target list across GitHub / npm / AWS / 1Password / HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes / Anthropic Claude Code. Rationale: Implements the credential-harvest signature documented in the article (the payload 'read .env files') and corroborated by StepSecurity / nrwl postmortem (targets npm, GitHub, AWS, 1Password, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, Anthropic Claude Code). The 5-distinct-paths-in-5-minutes threshold catches the burst behaviour while suppressing normal developer dotenv usage which typically touches 1-2 files. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running a legit credential-rotation or `aws configure` flow that touches multiple cred files in quick succession
  • Backup/sync tool (Dropbox, OneDrive, Time Machine) re-indexing a dotfile-heavy home directory under a node.exe context
  • CI runner agent (GitHub Actions self-hosted, GitLab runner) seeding multiple credentials at job start
  • IaC tooling (Terraform, Pulumi) using node-based providers that read AWS + kube + npm configs together
  • Repo-search / code-intel extensions (e.g. ripgrep wrappers, source-graph) scanning workspaces that legitimately contain .env files
Suppression filter
| where Cmd !contains "aws configure" and Cmd !contains "gh auth" and Cmd !contains "terraform" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" and not (DeviceName startswith "ci-runner-" or DeviceName startswith "gha-runner-")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine + parent process. If parent=Code.exe and the node process has no obvious workspace package.json invocation context, treat as suspicious. Capture the dropped output files (often staged in %TEMP%, ~/.npm/_npx, or /tmp) and hash them. 2. Contain: isolate the host, terminate the node process tree, rotate every credential class seen in the file list (GitHub PAT, npm, AWS, Claude Code, 1Password recovery, Vault). 3. Hunt: pivot AccountName across the fleet for the same 5-in-5min pattern, search DNS for git-service.com beacons from the same host in the same window, and audit GitHub Enterprise / npm / AWS CloudTrail for any privileged action using the rotated credentials in the prior 7 days.
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token", @".gitconfig"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","config","vault-token"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper.exe")
| where (FolderPath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (FileName in~ (CredFileNames) and FolderPath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)), SamplePaths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @".npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","vault-token"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (TargetFileName in~ (CredFileNames) and TargetFilePath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
  by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Code\ -\ Insiders.exe OR *\\Code\ Helper.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.env OR *\\.envrc OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.kube\\config OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.config\\1Password* OR *\\.docker\\config.json OR *vault-token*) -@TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\*
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node(\.exe)?|Code(\.exe)?|Code - Insiders\.exe|Code Helper(\.exe)?)$/i
| regex("\\\\\\.env$|\\\\\\.envrc$|\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|/\\.aws/credentials|\\\\\\.npmrc|/\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|/\\.kube/config|\\\\\\.claude\\\\settings\\.json|/\\.claude/settings\\.json|\\\\\\.config\\\\1Password|/\\.config/1Password|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|vault-token", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName!=/node_modules/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=distinct_hits))
| distinct_hits>=5

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as touched_files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.env*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".envrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_name="vault-token") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 5
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as touched_files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.env*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".envrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_name="vault-token") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 5
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.

DeviceFileEvents

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod or curl.exe against Discord webhooks for legitimate notifications
  • Game launchers (non-Discord) embedding Discord rich-presence calls via custom binaries
  • Custom helpdesk bots calling Discord API from a scheduled task using powershell.exe
  • Security tools that fetch indicator feeds from Discord-hosted gists
  • First-party Discord beta builds with non-standard EXE names
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhooks/","@everyone","slash-command") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("devops","build-bot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if it's a script interpreter spawned by Office, browser, or unknown parent, escalate. Validate the user's intent (do they own a Discord bot script?). 2) Contain — isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill the InitiatingProcessId, and block the destination Discord channel ID at the proxy if extractable from packet capture. 3) Hunt — search 30 days for the same parent-process hash across the estate, pivot on InitiatingProcessFolderPath for staged binaries, and query DeviceFileEvents for any GitHub-staged droppers (SoftEther, iox, frp) on the same host.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc
title: EchoCreep Discord C2 from Non-Browser Process
id: 8a4b9c1e-2d6f-4b13-8e0a-21a35b3f3771
description: Detects EchoCreep (Webworm APT, 2025) backdoor C2 traffic to Discord APIs initiated by a script interpreter or non-browser binary.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_dst:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'discord.com'
      - 'discordapp.com'
      - 'discord.gg'
      - 'cdn.discordapp.com'
  filter_legit_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\Discord.exe'
      - '\DiscordPTB.exe'
      - '\DiscordCanary.exe'
      - '\slack.exe'
      - '\Teams.exe'
      - '\Spotify.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
  condition: selection_dst and not filter_legit_image
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*discord.com OR *discordapp.com OR *discord.gg OR *cdn.discordapp.com) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\Discord.exe OR *\\DiscordPTB.exe OR *\\DiscordCanary.exe OR *\\slack.exe OR *\\Slack.exe OR *\\Teams.exe OR *\\Spotify.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\opera.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest (DomainName=/discord(app)?\.com$/i OR DomainName=/discord\.gg$/i OR DomainName=/cdn\.discordapp\.com$/i)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|cscript|wscript|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count >= 3
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com") OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*discord.com/api/v9/*","*discord.com/api/v10/*","*discordapp.com/api/*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\chrome.exe","*\\msedge.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\brave.exe","*\\opera.exe","*\\iexplore.exe","*\\Discord.exe","*\\DiscordPTB.exe","*\\DiscordCanary.exe","*\\Spotify.exe","*\\slack.exe","*\\Teams.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls dc(_time) as connection_buckets by src,user,process_name,dest | where conn_count>=3
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com") OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*discord.com/api/v9/*","*discord.com/api/v10/*","*discordapp.com/api/*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\chrome.exe","*\\msedge.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\brave.exe","*\\opera.exe","*\\iexplore.exe","*\\Discord.exe","*\\DiscordPTB.exe","*\\DiscordCanary.exe","*\\Spotify.exe","*\\slack.exe","*\\Teams.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls dc(_time) as connection_buckets by src,user,process_name,dest | where conn_count>=3
GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process AICommand & Control High
Hunts GraphWorm backdoor C2: Microsoft Graph API calls to /createUploadSession and victim-specific OneDrive directories from a non-Office, non-Edge process. ESET observed GraphWorm exclusively using OneDrive endpoints to fetch jobs and upload large staged files, with a separate directory per victim. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused endpoint: 'the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /createUploadSession to upload large, staged files' and confines GraphWorm to OneDrive paths per-victim. Excluding native Office/OneDrive/Edge processes preserves the malicious signal while suppressing legit Graph use. Cross-referenced MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002 and Microsoft's Graph API consumer list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PowerShell scripts using Microsoft Graph SDK for legitimate SharePoint/OneDrive automation
  • Backup or DLP agents using custom EXEs to enumerate user OneDrive content via Graph
  • Developer testing of /createUploadSession via Postman renamed to a custom binary
  • Power Automate Desktop using a bespoke runtime that hits Graph endpoints
  • Identity governance tools doing user-drive inventory via Graph
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pwsh.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Microsoft.Graph","Connect-MgGraph","Invoke-MgGraphRequest") and InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("itadmin","sharepoint-svc"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — review InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent for legitimate dev/admin context; check if the user has Graph SDK installed or scheduled tasks calling Graph. 2) Contain — isolate device, kill the offending process tree, revoke OAuth tokens scoped to Files.ReadWrite for that user via AAD audit. 3) Hunt — enumerate AADSignInEventsBeta for the same user's Graph token issuance, search for victim-specific OneDrive directories created via Office365 OneDrive audit logs, and pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 to find GraphWorm sibling implants estate-wide.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
   and (RemoteUrl has "createUploadSession" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/items" or RemoteUrl has "/drives/" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/root:")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","ONENOTE.EXE","Outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let GraphTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has "graph.microsoft.com"
       and (Url has "createUploadSession" or Url has "/me/drive/items" or Url has "/drives/" or Url has "/me/drive/root:")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
GraphTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| order by FirstNet desc

WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts contact with the compromised Amazon S3 buckets Webworm uses to stage configs, VM snapshots, mRemoteNG XMLs and SharpSecretsdump. Article names two buckets — wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com — used both for retrieving WormFrp configurations and exfiltrating data from victims in Italy and Spain. Rationale: Article cites exact bucket FQDNs (wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com). Any host in our estate touching these substrings is high-fidelity Webworm contact — the buckets are publicly documented IOCs taken down by ESET. No baseline exclusions needed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform fetching IOC samples from the same buckets after takedown (post-takedown re-resolution attempts)
  • SIEM enrichment lookup hitting the bucket name as DNS query when validating ingested IOCs
  • Security researcher revisiting the bucket from a corporate sandbox
  • DNS sinkhole appliance generating echo responses for blocked IOC FQDNs
  • VirusTotal Retro-Hunt notification webhook including the URL in payload
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("misp-modules.exe","opencti.exe","yara.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("misp","opencti","threatfox","virustotal-retrohunt"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the initiating process, account, and full URL path; if response code is 200 and bytes >0, treat as confirmed retrieval. Determine whether host downloaded WormFrp config or uploaded VM snapshots/credentials. 2) Contain — isolate host, kill the requesting process, block both bucket FQDNs at proxy/DNS, and rotate any credentials touched on that host (especially mRemoteNG saved profiles). 3) Hunt — search DeviceFileEvents for SharpSecretsdump, iox, frp, SoftEther, mRemoteNG XML exports written in the last 30 days; pivot DeviceNetworkEvents to the known Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs (45.77.13.67, 64.176.85.158, 104.243.23.43, 108.61.200.151, 144.168.60.233) from the same host.
let WebwormBuckets = dynamic(["wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com","whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com","wamanharipethe.s3.amazonaws.com"]);
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| union (
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where AdditionalFields has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings) or RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RemoteUrl,tostring(AdditionalFields)), RemoteIP, RemotePort=toint(0), ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Destination=Name, Detail=tostring(QueryType)
),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or RequestURL has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Destination=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Detail=RequestURL
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstHostname has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=DstHostname, Detail=Url
),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where HttpHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=HttpHostName, Detail=Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes AICommand & Control Medium
Atomic IOC match for the five Webworm C2 IPs (Vultr / IT7 Networks) and the six SHA1 hashes published by ESET for WormFrp, ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormSocket, EchoCreep, and GraphWorm samples observed in 2025. Rationale: Direct atomic IOC match on values published in the ESET article: five Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs and six SHA1 hashes. The article ties the Vultr/IT7 IP block to confirmed Webworm proxy/VPN infrastructure (article: 'All Webworm proxies and VPN services are cloud servers that belong to network infrastructure controlled by Vultr and IT7 Networks'). Zero baseline contact expected in a benign estate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform downloading the same SHA1 indicators from VT/MISP and writing them to local disk for enrichment
  • Researcher analyst sandbox detonating the published sample for verification
  • Red-team purple exercise replaying Webworm samples for SOC tuning
  • DNS sinkhole/IDS reflecting decoy traffic back into the same telemetry pipeline
  • Legitimate Vultr-hosted SaaS that incidentally shares an IP with one of the five (verify CIDR before suppression)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe","yara.exe","virustotal.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("download_sample","vt-cli","misp-modules"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm the IOC was hit by a production endpoint (not researcher/sandbox tag) and capture full process / file / network context; pull PCAP if available. 2) Contain — isolate host(s) via EDR, kill matching processes, quarantine matching binaries on disk, block all five IPs at perimeter, and add the hashes to AV/EDR custom-IOC list. 3) Hunt — sweep last 90 days estate-wide for any of the six hashes, the two S3 buckets (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers), Discord API / Graph /createUploadSession beaconing patterns, and SoftEther/iox/frp binaries on disk; review GitHub repo `github.com/anjsdgasdf/WordPress` artifact downloads.
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (WebwormIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=SHA1, RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,InitiatingProcessSHA1), RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc

let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
